stories.head: AI-generated answers now top starting point for product research among AI-active shoppers
stories.plain: Impact.com research finds 47% of AI-active U.S. consumers now begin product searches with an AI-generated answer, outpacing traditional search at 26%. This reshapes where brands must show up — not just on Google, but inside AI responses — making generative engine optimization a budget-level decision, not a future experiment.

stories.head: What to do before buying a martech platform with AI context
stories.plain: Practical pre-purchase checklist for AI-enabled martech: define what content is approved, what's off-limits, and who has final authority over AI-generated decisions before signing a contract. Directly addresses how governance gaps cause costly regrets post-implementation — essential reading for anyone evaluating platforms this budget cycle.

stories.head: How AI agents help improve your customer experience
stories.plain: A practical guide to deploying agentic AI in customer-facing roles, covering where agents genuinely reduce friction versus where they frustrate customers. Useful for teams deciding which CX workflows to automate, and what guardrails to put in place before handing decisions to an agent.

stories.head: Brandi AI CEO on winning the AI answer, not the click
stories.plain: Leah Nurik explains how AI assistants decide which brand names to surface, why GEO requires combining PR, product marketing, and structured data — not just SEO tricks — and what metrics replace traditional rank tracking. Actionable for any marketer whose budget still assumes Google is the main discovery channel.

stories.head: Parloa survey: only 7% of travelers would let AI act autonomously on their behalf
stories.plain: Despite openness to AI monitoring trips, consumer willingness to grant autonomous action stays at just 7% — a critical trust gap for brands building agentic customer-service tools. Younger travelers show sharply higher acceptance, signaling where the ceiling will rise first and how to phase agentic rollouts by segment.

stories.head: Salesforce buying AI customer support company Cresta
stories.plain: Salesforce is acquiring Cresta, which builds AI voice agents for live customer calls. The deal plugs real-time conversation intelligence directly into CRM data and Salesforce's Agentforce platform. This reshapes how enterprise contact-centre AI is bought — bundled with CRM rather than purchased as a point solution — raising the bar for standalone vendors.

stories.head: AI-generated answers now top starting point for product research among AI-active shoppers
stories.plain: Impact.com research finds 47% of AI-active U.S. consumers started their last product search with an AI-generated answer, beating traditional search at 26%. This is a structural shift in discovery that forces marketers to rethink where budgets go and makes Generative Engine Optimization a commercial priority, not an experiment.

stories.head: What to do before buying a martech platform with AI context
stories.plain: A practical pre-purchase checklist for marketing teams evaluating AI-enabled platforms — covering what content and data the AI is allowed to use, who approves outputs, and how guardrails are enforced. Directly relevant to governance decisions that must happen before a contract is signed, not after deployment reveals the gaps.

stories.head: AI traffic drives 83% more revenue per visit, Adobe research finds
stories.plain: Adobe's data shows visitors arriving from AI assistants convert 90% better and generate 83% more revenue per visit than non-AI traffic. This gives marketers concrete ROI justification for investing in GEO and content strategies aimed at AI answer engines, changing how channel attribution and budget allocation should be framed.

stories.head: Brandi AI CEO on winning the AI answer, not the click
stories.plain: Leah Nurik explains how AI assistants choose which vendors to name, why GEO requires PR and product marketing to work together, and what metrics replace traditional rank tracking. Actionable for anyone building a brand visibility strategy in a world where the AI answer, not the search result page, is the new front door.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI agents are rewriting the purchase journey
body: AI-generated answers have displaced search engines as the primary starting point for product research among active AI users, and traffic arriving via AI referrals already converts at 83% higher revenue per visit than traditional organic traffic. The implication is structural: the funnel no longer begins with a keyword query on a results page.

Brands that optimise only for clicks rather than for being cited inside an AI answer risk invisibility at the moment of highest commercial intent. As Brandi AI CEO Leah Nurik frames it, the new goal is 'winning the answer, not the click' — a complete inversion of two decades of SEO logic.

themes.head: Consumer trust is the hard ceiling on AI autonomy
body: Survey after survey reveals the same gap: consumers are curious about AI assistance but deeply reluctant to hand over control. Only 7% of travellers would let AI act autonomously on their behalf, and Talkdesk's retail research shows enterprise AI ambitions consistently outrun the trust consumers are willing to extend.

This is not a temporary friction — it is a structural ceiling on agentic deployment. Marketers who push full automation without earning incremental trust will trigger backlash; those who design for human confirmation at key moments will compound adoption gradually and sustainably.

themes.head: The AI ROI proof gap is becoming a governance crisis
body: Most marketers report that AI is working, yet few can produce evidence that holds up to CFO scrutiny — a disconnect that is shifting from an embarrassment into a budget and procurement risk. Without measurement infrastructure, AI spend looks indistinguishable from faith-based marketing.

The practitioner guidance emerging in response stresses that strategic intent must precede the prompt: organisations need a destination for AI output before they can measure whether it arrived. Buying yet another AI-layer platform without that foundation compounds the proof gap rather than closing it.

themes.head: Platform consolidation accelerates around agentic CX stacks
body: Salesforce's acquisition of Cresta is the clearest signal yet that the major CRM & CX platforms are racing to own the full agentic loop — not just provide AI features, but absorb specialised AI capability so agents can act end-to-end without leaving the core platform. Bolt-on AI is giving way to built-in AI.

Teamily AI's vision of an 'agentic, appless world' points in the same direction: the app layer itself may compress as agents orchestrate tasks across services. For marketers, the near-term decision is whether to consolidate into an emerging mega-platform or preserve best-of-breed flexibility before exits close.

Agile Brand · Asana agentic work management

themes.head: Human judgement remains the irreplaceable last mile
body: A consistent counter-current runs through this month's practitioner writing: AI surfaces patterns, optimises channels, and executes at scale — but it cannot supply strategic meaning, brand values, or competitive self-awareness. 'If you don't define your weakness, AI will' captures the risk of passive adoption.

The same tension appears in SEO: blindly optimising for AI ranking signals rather than genuine user value creates fragile visibility that algorithms can revoke. Marketers who treat AI as a co-pilot rather than an autopilot retain the interpretive layer that turns data into defensible decisions.

month.takeaway: Every major signal this month points to the same underlying tension: AI can automate the execution layer completely, but trust, meaning, and proof remain stubbornly human responsibilities — and organisations that skip that layer will find their AI investments both unmeasurable and unaccepted.
